stem: 3% NaCl is used for:

B_reason: 3% is not routine maintenance.
C_reason: K has specific solutions.
D_choice: Severe hyponatremia and cerebral edema (draws water out of cells)
D_reason: Hypertonic saline pulls water intravascularly for severe hypoNa/cerebral edema.

stem: D5W after dextrose metabolism behaves as:
A_reason: Not permanently isotonic.
B_reason: Colloids are proteins/starches.
C_reason: D5W is initially isotonic then becomes hypotonic as glucose metabolizes.

stem: Lactated Ringer's is classified as:
A_reason: LR approximates plasma osmolality for expansion.
B_reason: LR is not a blood product.
C_reason: Hypertonic is 3%/5% NaCl etc.

stem: Colloid IV fluids primary use
A_reason: Colloids expand intravascular volume via oncotic pressure.
B_reason: KCl is separate electrolyte replacement.
C_choice: Plasma volume expansion in hemorrhage/severe hypovolemia
C_reason: Used for hemorrhage/severe hypovolemia in teaching.

stem: Surgical asepsis means:
A_reason: Single-use vials should not be routinely reused.
B_choice: Sterile field and sterile technique to prevent microorganism entry to tissues
B_reason: Asepsis prevents microbes entering sterile tissues.

stem: Time-out (surgical safety) verifies:
A_reason: Universal protocol/time-out confirms identity, site, procedure.

B_reason: Music is irrelevant to safety pause.
C_reason: Not part of timeout.
D_reason: Billing is administrative later.

stem: PACU priority assessment mnemonic focus:

D_choice: Airway, breathing, circulation, surgical site, vitals

stem: Post-op fever within first 24 hours is often due to:
A_reason: Wound infection peaks later; early fever often atelectasis/inflammation.

stem: IV infiltration sign:
A_choice: Cool skin, tight edema, slowed infusion at site
A_reason: Local coolness, swelling, and poor flow suggest infiltration.
B_reason: Bilateral edema is systemic, not catheter-related.
C_reason: Fever is not classic infiltration.
D_reason: Chest pain unrelated.

stem: Phlebitis at IV site priority:
A_reason: Tourniquet is not routine phlebitis care.
B_reason: Continuing irritant line worsens phlebitis.
C_choice: Remove or rotate line per protocol; elevate limb; warm compress if ordered
C_reason: Discontinue/rotate and supportive care per policy.
D_reason: Vigorous massage can spread infection/thrombus.

stem: NPO before elective surgery primary reason:
A_reason: Aspiration risk drops with empty stomach per perioperative teaching.
B_choice: Increase thirst for IV fluids only
B_reason: Thirst is side effect, not primary purpose.
C_reason: Bowel sounds return post-op.

stem: Elective vs emergency surgery distinction:
A_reason: Elective is planned/scheduled.

stem: Pre-op teaching should include:

stem: Hypertonic 10% dextrose (D10W) effect:
A_reason: Hypertonic dextrose draws fluid into the intravascular space.

stem: WHO surgical hand scrub aims to:
A_choice: Reduce resident and transient flora on hands before sterile procedure
A_reason: Transient/resident flora reduction is the goal.

stem: Post-op paralytic ileus nursing care includes:

B_reason: NG and gradual diet per orders are standard.

stem: IV gauge selection: large bore used when:

stem: Central line vs peripheral line: central access allows:
A_choice: CVP monitoring, irritant meds, long-term TPN access per orders
A_reason: Peripheral lines limit vesicants/rate.

stem: Sterile gowning/gloving sequence taught in skills lab:

C_reason: Gown then gloves is standard taught order (follow lab policy).
D_choice: Gloves before gown always without teaching variation
D_reason: Policy may vary slightly but contamination is always avoided.

stem: OPET (outpatient surgery) discharge criteria include:
A_choice: Drive immediately after general anesthesia alone
A_reason: Driving after GA is unsafe initially.
B_reason: Pain must be controlled/managed.
C_reason: Teaching is mandatory.

D_reason: Stable ABCs, voiding, escort, and teaching are standard OPET discharge anchors.

stem: KCl IV never given:
A_choice: Mixed in 500 mL NS per protocol
A_reason: Diluted infusion is correct route.
B_reason: Must be diluted and rate-limited per policy.
C_reason: Oral/enteral preferred when possible.
D_choice: Diluted slow peripheral infusion per policy

stem: Air embolism prevention with central line:
A_reason: Air must never be infused.

B_reason: Clamp/de-air lines; left lateral decubitus if air embolus suspected.
